name: George Francis Adams (#1)

Served in the Confederate army during the Civil War under Generals Price, Van Dorn, and McGruder

Per the 1898 biography: farmed in Jefferson County, VA, then moved to Chariton County, MO onto War of 1812 grant prairie land; pre-empted 160 acres at 12.5 cents an acre, built up to a full section devoted to stock, served as justice of the peace, came to Colorado in 1886 and lived retired until his death at 81.

DPBR sketch of his son (naming him 'George P.'): born in Jefferson County, Va., farmed there until 1827, then removed to Chariton County, Mo., settling on prairie land set aside for War of 1812 land grants.
DPBR: bought and sold a land-grant tract, pre-empted another 160 acres at 12.5 cents per acre, took another similar tract, improved the land for the stock business and eventually owned a section.
DPBR: served as justice of the peace.

Listed as minor son of Josee P. Adams in the will written in 1830 (about 13 years old) [Bill Allen, Descendants of Jose Pierre Adams, 2011, line 4000]

Preparer's note: the biography's name 'George P.' is wrong (it was George Francis), and a move to Missouri in 1827 is unlikely; he most likely arrived late 1840 or early 1841 (first Chariton County record is the 1850 census). [Bill Allen, Descendants of Jose Pierre Adams, 2011, line 4370]
Obituary: he left four sons and four daughters; raised his children under his own care after his wife's death. [Bill Allen, Further Research, 2012, line 6846]
Only land patent record for George in Chariton County: 1857, an 80-acre parcel, a homestead purchase rather than a military land warrant. [Bill Allen, Further Research, 2012, line 7011]
The 1857 parcel was part of the land warrant granted in 1851 to his father-in-law, John S. Lane. [Bill Allen, Further Research, 2012, line 7089]
Described as the eldest child of Jose1's family. [Bill Allen, Further Research, 2012, line 7344]
His obituary says the family came west in 1833. [Bill Allen, Further Research, 2012, line 7362]
The Gill biography says he was a twin of his sister Mary, and both were deceased by 1909. [Bill Allen, Further Research, 2012, line 7598]
Twin brother of Mary Adams (Swan) [Bill Allen, Further Research, 2012, line 8313]
Named as a cousin, under 21, in the will of Francis A. HAMILTON [Bill Allen, Further Research, 2012, line 9703]
Francis Hamilton's will left him a small sum when he was an adolescent. [Bill Allen, Descendants of Jose Pierre Adams, 2011, line 2913]
